To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase diagram of a nanoalloy is a set of phase diagrams attached to surface sites or inner layers and that the driving force of a phase transition is not the same for the core and the surface of an alloy.

(i) the Wulff polyhedron (PW) of 405 atoms (PW405) in the Cu-Ag system, characterized by a large size difference of the constituent atoms and a tendency to demixing, exhibits three different types of transitions, namely, (a) a structural transition, (b) a demixing transition, and (c) a transition to the Janus structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the coupling between chemical and structural orders in binary nanoalloys.
the understanding of the structure and the order in bimetallic nanoparticles.
the development of the phase diagrams of nanoalloys, i.e. of small particles composed of several hundreds to several thousands atoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work provides a complete description of the structure and phase diagrams of the Cu-Ag binary system at the nanoscale, and that this description can be used as a guideline to design new nanoscale materials with specific properties.
we have shown how the phase diagram of a nanoalloy can be constructed by combining the results of two different thermodynamic ensembles (pseudo grand canonical and canonical).

we have demonstrated the existence of a nano phase diagram for a bimetallic system with strong size effects, which can be described as a collection of different phase diagrams, each one attached to a specific surface or inner site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach, the so-called pseudo grand canonical ensemble, to study the phase diagram of nanosystems.
we have been able to establish the first phase diagram for a nanoalloy, i.e. the polyhedron with 405 atoms (PW405), in the Cu-Ag binary system.
we have developed a methodology to establish phase diagrams of nanosystems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to describe a phase diagram of a nanoalloy, one needs to consider the different types of sites that exist in the particle.
the phase diagram of nanoclusters is not the same as the one of the bulk material, even if the same chemical species constitute both phases.
a nanoalloy is not a single phase but an ensemble of phases, each phase being associated with a specific class of sites.
